query: Consider the following context: During the hot dip aluminum plating process, components such as sinking rollers, pulling rollers, and guide plates will come into long-term contact with high-temperature liquid aluminum and be corroded by the aluminum liquid, greatly reducing their service life. In that context, which material can be used for prepare parts for the dipping and plating equipment and protect the equipment from erosion, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Replacing conventional alloy parts with tungsten carbide-based cermets for hot-dip aluminum plating equipment will mitigate corrosion and wear in long-term exposure to high-temperature molten aluminum.
generation.material_initial_state: Equipment components (e.g., rollers, guide plates) are conventionally made of steel or iron-based alloys that rapidly corrode in molten aluminum.
generation.intervention: Fabricate and install tungsten carbide-based cermet parts (via powder metallurgy or infiltration techniques) to directly contact the molten aluminum.
generation.conditions: Continuous operation at typical molten aluminum temperatures (~680–710 °C) with prolonged exposure to corrosive aluminum bath conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: Tungsten carbide phases in the cermet remain stable and chemically inert against molten aluminum, thereby reducing reactions and intermetallic formation.
generation.mechanism: The thermodynamic stability of tungsten carbide at high temperature and negligible chemical reactivity with aluminum help slow down dissolution rates and mitigate chemical attack, thus reducing corrosion and erosion of the parts.
generation.predicted_outcome: Service life of molten-aluminum-contacting components is significantly extended compared to iron- or steel-based alloys (e.g., an approximate factor of 2×–3× longer life) due to improved corrosion and erosion resistance.
generation.baseline: Steel or iron-based alloy parts currently have shortened service life due to rapid corrosion/erosion in molten aluminum.
generation.boundary: Production cost and specialized fabrication processes for cermets could limit widespread use; long-term field performance data under extreme service conditions remain limited.
generation.uncertainty: Exact quantitative data on lifespan extension and performance under all industrial conditions are not fully established by the supplied evidence; further testing is required.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare test coupons from tungsten carbide-based cermets and from a reference steel. Expose both sets to molten aluminum at standard hot-dip temperatures over prolonged intervals.
measurements: Surface microstructure using SEM and EDS
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If tungsten carbide-based cermet samples exhibit similar or higher rates of corrosion/erosion as the reference steel, the hypothesis is disproven.
